title: Normalized derived signed-line reductions and support
statement: Fix ell, E, X, a completed coefficient line L, and ordinary comparison isomorphisms b satisfying PowerFormula [def-pur-integral-line-reduction-data]. There are natural isomorphisms d(m,n): ordinaryTensor(L^[m]) followed by derived reduction_n ≅ derived reduction_n followed by finite ordinary tensor with reduction_n(L)^[m]. They satisfy DerivedFormula: on every good K-flat flat-term representative the chain map is balancing followed by b, agrees with d through the actual reduction counit and specified tensor representative comparisons, and commutes with the strict quotient transitions with TransitionFormula. For every unbounded K, every interval [a,z] containing all cohomological supports of its derived reductions also contains all cohomological supports of the derived reductions of its ordinary twist.

Proof (3), last sentence interpreted in the derived-complete integral coefficient convention; extracted generic reduction/restriction argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-line-unbounded-derived-tensor] to $P$ over $R$ and to the rank-one $P_n$ over $R_n$. These degree-zero lines are K-flat, ordinary tensor computes their unbounded derived tensor, and their cohomology functors are ordinary tensor on cohomology sheaves. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to the identity topos with ring map $R\to R_n$. It gives $(K\otimes_R^LP)_n\cong K_n\otimes_{R_n}^L(P\otimes_RR_n)$, then compose with the given normalized ordinary power comparison b. On a K-flat representative $U$ with flat terms its degree-$j$ map is the balancing identification $(U^j\otimes_RP)\otimes_RR_n\cong(U^j\otimes_RR_n)\otimes_{R_n}P_n$. Its inverse multiplies the two quotient scalars. Consequently these comparisons are compatible with the strict quotient transitions as well as natural in $K$.

For every $n$ and $i$, the preceding derived reduction comparison and [lem-pur-line-unbounded-derived-tensor] over $R_n$ give $\mathcal H^i((K\otimes_R^LP)_n)\cong\mathcal H^i(K_n)\otimes_{R_n}P_n$. If $i\notin[a,b]$, the right hand side is zero whenever $\mathcal H^i(K_n)=0$. Thus any common interval $[a,b]$ remains a common interval, with exactly the same endpoints, in the meaning of [def-weil-cohomological-support]. This argument uses cohomological support, not Tor amplitude or a boundedness assumption on the original unbounded representative.
